comment: PR body table: TAM dates 85.0 vs BM25 46.0 at FC-SH 262k (single runs, temp 0.7; TAM run range 85-86 given, none for BM25). Caveat: a later PR comment (2026-09-24) shows the rank-order adapter mislabeled recency; v14.5.1 recorded-order gives 91/92, so the PR-body numbers are superseded.

Table 3 gpt-4o-mini block: SH 0.738 vs 0.635, average SubEM over 6k/32k/64k/262k. Own ablation.
Table 7: 95% vs 69% (6k SH). Minor flag issue: the paper states 95% binomial intervals of about +/-10 pts per FC cell and uses McNemar/bootstrap on LME, so unc is closer to 'partial' than 'no'.

Table 2: Single-Doc 0.760 vs 0.740. Table 7 RULER-QA1/2 = 2 instances x 100 Q, so 100 per set.

Table 2 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B block: MH F1 15.27 vs Zep 12.77, pooled over 4 lengths (100 MH each). Note: the model is not named in the row. Paper claims highest avg F1 in all 12 configs. No CI for this pairwise comparison (CIs only for the matched top-8 control).
Table 2: InfBench 0.153 vs 0.129 (100 instances x 1 Q).

Values match Table 3 (MH 0.180 vs MemoRAG 0.070), but the baseline is not a 4-length average. MemoRAG 7.0 = MAB main-table FC-MH, which is the 262K split only (MAB Table 2: 262K, 1:100). The paper's other copied rows confirm this: Mem0 0.18/0.02 = MAB per-length 262K values. The comparison is length-mismatched (avg of 6k-262k vs 262k-only), so the baseline n is 100 and the gap is not like-for-like.
Table 2: ReFind MH-QA 69.0 vs HippoRAG 2 66.0 (copied from MAB, GPT-4o-mini). Claims highest mean accuracy. Uncertainty (+/-std) only on LME-S/M subsets, not on the MAB suite.
PR body: 82.0 vs 71.0 at FC-SH 6k. Run ranges 80-84 vs 71-72. Later comment: the dates/no-dates gap was partly an adapter rank-ordering artifact; in recorded order 14.5.1 gives 100 vs 98.
Table 2 Qwen3.5-9B: overall F1 45.45 vs A-Mem 40.66 over 800 Q (SH+MH x 4 lengths).

Values match Table 3 (gpt-5-mini SH 0.920 vs Infini Memory 0.800). copied should be 'yes': 80.0/22.0/51.0 are exactly Infini Memory-H in 2606.10677 Table 1. That source uses a GPT-5 LLM judge (not SubEM) and does not state the FC lengths (likely the MAB-standard 262K config), so metric and n are not matched with MindMemOS's 4-length SubEM average.
Table 7: 11% vs 8% (262k MH). The paper itself calls this within noise. Flag: unc should be partial (the paper gives a generic +/-10 pt 95% binomial interval per cell), not merely informal.

Table 3: overall 0.585 vs 0.510. Same issue as row 12: the Infini number is copied from 2606.10677 (LLM-judge metric, unspecified FC length), so copied should be 'yes' and the comparison is not metric- or length-matched.
Table 1 Qwen2.5-7B: MemAB-FC MH 0.642 vs RAG 0.040, pooled over 4 lengths. RAG is TF-IDF top-50 facts. McNemar tests are reported.
Table 4: MAB-64k 41.0 vs 27.0 without recall (same snapshot). Table 8 shows these are MH questions.
Table 2 SmolLM3-3B: 20.21 vs delta-Mem 20.13. The paper states 3,671 Q / 14 datasets, sample-weighted (mixed metrics). 3671 = 100+100+300+1500+5x100+200+100+71+800, i.e. EventQA = 1500 Q, not 500.
Table 3 (InEp-Know, DeepSeek-V3.2): Ruler qa1 Mem0 75.00 vs BM25 73.00. Benchmark paper with no SOTA claim. AR total of 2000 again implies EventQA = 1500.
642/800 = 80.25% vs Gemini 2.5 Pro 75.0% (600/800). Exact CIs reported. Caveat: the 800 Q come from only 4 fact lists, and the paper's four-list interval is 67.3-92.8, so effective n << 800.
Table 8: DetectiveQA 85.9 (61/71) vs Letta 82.4. 82.4 is not k/71 (58/71 = 81.7, 59/71 = 83.1), which suggests Letta was scored on fewer items (e.g. 56/68) or per-novel averaging. Minor.

Table 4: CMC FC-SH 95.0 vs published GPT-5-mini 78.0 (MAB 262K split). The paper says published rows are 'reference; readers differ and they are not bolded against this work', so it disclaims this comparison. Its SOTA claim covers FC multi-hop only, so sota = no for an SH row is defensible.
Text: resolver 88/36 at 262K vs camera-ready GPT-5-mini 78/28. The paper calls this 'a reading aid, not a leaderboard' (whole-list reading vs chunked ingestion). Exact CIs given.
Issue table: FC-MH 64K 8.0 vs 6.0 (GPT-4.1-mini). The issue headline is MH average 12 vs 5 (n=400).

Table 3: Recall@5 0.14 vs 0.10 on 25 recsys queries. sota yes is right ('highest observed scores on MAB'). unc = yes is overstated for this row: paired tests and bootstrap CIs are only for LoCoMo. For MAB the text just says the difference 'is not significant', with no test reported.
Issue #20 (duplicated in #21 with the same numbers): 262k public-transfer 27/100 -> 44/100, explicitly not an official score.
